content.text: The insurance clause exists and is asymmetrically favorable to us. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance.
input.rationale: An insurance clause is present at § 14.6, so the rule is satisfied rather than missing. It obliges each Party (including RevMed) to carry insurance appropriate to its activities, expressly including product liability cover — the risk that matters in this clinical development/commercialization collaboration, as opposed to a hosting or data-processing engagement. It also gives us certificates/evidence on request and, one-way in our favour, requires RevMed to notify Sanofi ahead of cancellation, non-renewal or material change. Two further provisions run in our favour and should not be disturbed: Sanofi may satisfy the requirement through self-insurance, and insurance is expressly not a cap on either Party's Article XIV indemnification obligations. The clause sets limits by reference to "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" rather than the preferred stated figures (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M); we note that as a sub-element short of preferred wording, not a material failure, given this is a bilateral pharma collaboration in which RevMed does not process Customer Data or work on our premises, so the cyber/E&O-driven fallback limits are not the operative exposure. Effectively at the fallback: a substantive, mutual insurance covenant with evidence and cancellation-notice mechanics, but without express dollar limits. No redline proposed.
